h3. Description

When you schedule a technician for the morning, the Schedule shows the job in the afternoon. A one-hour job put on a technician's calendar for 9:00 in the morning appears on the board, in the pop-up summary and in the shift window as 3:00 in the afternoon. Every time on the page is shifted by six hours - the block position, the hover summary, the start and end times in the shift window, and the little 'now' marker in Day view. A twelve-hour day shift that should read 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM instead reads 1:00 PM to 1:00 AM and spills over into the next day on the Day view. This makes the Schedule unusable as a planning board: nobody can tell a technician when to start, and a morning job looks like an evening job.

h3. Branch / Environment

Branch tested: https://sv8685.qa.shopview.com/schedule · API host: https://sv8685api.qa.shopview.com · Build marker (meta app-version): v3.5-4873abe · index.html last-modified Tue, 04 Aug 2026 14:47:39 GMT, etag 9b4b1fc776ebbfb04a9a0ca051d847f7 · Organisation d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f · Location: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a, timezone America/Edmonton) · Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Administrator) · Observed 2026-08-04, 16:00-19:00 UTC.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Open the Schedule and pick the Week view.
# Find the work order S-15855 Vuchester Retail, unit 10123073, line ' Service - Mobile service call made by George Donald 403-369-7067' in the left-hand list (type S-15855 into 'Search work orders').
# Drag that card onto the row for technician Ayesha Khan, on the Tuesday column.
# Note that Ayesha Khan's working hours in Edit Staff Member are Monday 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM and Tuesday to Friday 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, so the job should start at 7:00 in the morning.
# Hover the new block and read the time range in the pop-up summary.
# Click the block and read the two time boxes in the shift window.
# Switch to the Day view for that date and look at where the block sits against the hour labels, and at the time printed on the 'now' marker.

h3. Expected behaviour

The Schedule shows shop-local times. A job scheduled to start at 7:00 in the morning reads 7:00 AM everywhere - on the block, in the hover summary, in the shift window and in the Day view position. The 'now' marker matches the clock on the wall at the shop.

h3. Current behaviour

Every time is six hours later than it should be. The 7:00 AM job reads 1:00 PM; a 9:00 AM job reads 3:00 PM; the 'now' marker read 4:11 PM while the shop clock read 10:11 AM. The date can roll over too: a 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM shift reads 1:00 PM to 1:00 AM and is drawn partly on the following day.

h3. Images

No screenshot is attached. The evidence for this ticket is a captured DOM/state reading rather than a visual difference; the exact values are in the technical section below.

h3. Technical details for developers

The write path converts shop-local to UTC correctly and the read path never converts back, so UTC is rendered as wall-clock. Evidence: shift cea79194-02d3-46d1-958b-a76f17ee1cec is stored startsAt 2026-08-02T16:01:00Z (= 10:01 local, America/Edmonton is UTC-6) and the tooltip reads 'Sun, Aug 2, 2026 - 4:01 PM - 5:13 PM'. Creating a shift with startTime '09:00' via POST /api/schedule/shifts stored 15:00Z and the modal's native input[type=time] value attribute is literally '15:00'. This is NOT a client-locale artefact: forcing the browser timezone to America/Edmonton (the workplace's own timezone from GET /api/staff/my-workplaces) produced the identical wrong value. Affected surfaces: schedule_shift_block text_schedule_block_time, the hover card, input_shift_detail_start_time / input_shift_detail_end_time, text_schedule_now_time, and Day-view horizontal positioning.

The write path converts shop-local to UTC correctly and the read path never converts back, so UTC is rendered as wall-clock. Evidence: shift cea79194-02d3-46d1-958b-a76f17ee1cec is stored startsAt 2026-08-02T16:01:00Z (= 10:01 local, America/Edmonton is UTC-6) and the tooltip reads 'Sun, Aug 2, 2026 - 4:01 PM - 5:13 PM'. h2. 1 · Description

Each of the six new reports has a *Location* chooser in its toolbar, so a person can pick which branch or branches the report covers.

If somebody only has access to *one* branch, that chooser has nothing to choose. There is only ever one answer. The product owner has decided the chooser should simply not be shown to that person.

Right now it *is* shown — on *all six* reports. The person sees a control reading _"Location — All locations"_, with a clear button and a dropdown arrow, that cannot change anything about what they see.

*Why it matters:* it is a control that does nothing, offered to the people least able to make sense of it. It reads as though there is more data available somewhere and they have filtered it out, which prompts support questions. It is also the one place in the six reports where the product disagrees with the product owner's decision about who sees the location controls at all.

# Sign out, and sign in as *Wesley McClure*.
# Open *Reports* from the top navigation.
# Open *Sales By Customer* and look along the toolbar at the top right of the report, past the date range, *Product Type* and *Customer* controls.
# Do the same on *Sales By Representative*, *Parts Velocity*, *Technician Utilization*, *Work In Progress* and *Inventory Value*.
# Put Wesley McClure's role and location access back to *Technician* at **Staging Lethbridge - 4310**.

*Date range used:* each report's own default — *This Month* on Sales By Customer, Sales By Representative, Work In Progress and Inventory Value; *This Year* on Parts Velocity. The chooser is present on every one of them regardless, so the date range is not a factor.

*What was tried and ruled out:*

||Tried||Result||
|An administrator with access to *several* locations|Chooser shown — *correct*, this is the normal case|
|Wesley McClure with access to *one* location|Chooser *still shown* on all six — the defect|

|All six reports|Same result on all six, so it is not one report's toolbar|

h2. 4 · Expected behaviour

For a person who has access to only one location, the *Location* chooser is *not shown at all* on any of the six reports. The report simply shows that one location's data.

This is the product owner's decision, given on *2026-08-05*. He was shown what the product does today and asked which he wanted, and he chose:

{quote}
"Change the product to match your ruling - hide it."
{quote}

----

h2. 5 · Current behaviour

The *Location* chooser is present on *all six* reports for that person. It reads *"Location — All locations"* and carries a clear (×) button and a dropdown arrow. Opening it offers the single location they can reach.

The per-row *Location column* behaves correctly for the same person on five of the six reports — it is properly absent, because only one location is in view. So this is specifically about the *chooser*, not the column.

|With technicians selected and with none selected|Same four short labels either way|
|The button's position in the toolbar|*Correct* — leftmost, with the column-selection button immediately after it. Only the wording inside the menu is wrong|

----

h2. 4 · Expected behaviour

The Technician Utilization menu uses the same wording as the other reports:

* *Download Summary (PDF)*
* *Download Expanded View (PDF)*
* *Download Summary (CSV)*
* *Download Expanded View (CSV)*

But the menu holds FOUR items, not three: "Summary (PDF)", "Summary (CSV)", "Expanded (PDF)", "Expanded (CSV)" — no "Download" prefix anywhere, and a second CSV variant the spec does not describe.
{quote}

*Specification references.* Technician Utilization description, version 5 (2026-07-29): {{S7-R2}} _'an option labeled "Download Summary (PDF)"'_, {{S7-R3}} _'"Download Expanded View (PDF)"'_, {{S7-R4}} _'"Download (CSV)"'_. Sales By Customer version 13 {{S15-R1}}/{{S15-R2}} and Sales By Representative version 15 carry the longer four-item wording, which their builds match.

*A second, related question that is NOT part of this ticket, recorded so it is not lost.* The description for this report names *three* menu items; the build ships *four* — a separate spreadsheet option for the Summary and the Expanded views. The product owner's answer settles the *wording* in his own words but does not explicitly state the *count*; that the menu should end up with four is our reading of _"bring it into line with"_ the two reports he named, both of which offer four. *A one-word confirmation from him is outstanding*, so please treat the option count as his to confirm and the wording as decided.
